 :JUDGMENT:
This is a Claim Petition U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act claiming compensation of Rs.60,00,000/ for the death of Rathna Ram, in the road traffic accident.

2. The brief facts of the petition are as under:
On 26.11.2020 at about 9.20 a.m., Ratna Ram was proceeding as a rider on the Two Wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA19EY8857 from Jalahalli Cross towards 8 th Mile on NH4 by following all traffic rules.

When he reached near Spirit Zone, T. Dasarahalli,
the driver of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA435119 drove the vehicle from behind i.e., Jalahalli Cross, rash or negligently, with high speed in a ZigZag manner and dashed against the rare portion of two wheeler in which Ratna Ram was proceeding.
As a result of which, the Ratna Ram fell down from scooter, wheel of the lorry ran over his head and he succumbed to injuries on the spot.
Then the body of deceased Ratna Ram was shifted to Saptagiri Hospital, Bengaluru,

After postmortem,
body of deceased was handed over to petitioners, they have shifted the body to their village at Rajasthan.
The petitioners have spent Rs.2,00,000/ towards funeral and obsequies ceremonies of deceased.
It is stated that, due to sudden death of deceased, the petitioners have suffered mental shock and agony, they have lost love and affection of deceased.

At the time of accident, deceased was aged 22 years and he was working as a Sales Executive at Pipe Chem Industries, No.3/4, 1 st Main, Peenya 1st Stage, 1st Main Road, Peenya Industrial Area, Bengaluru and he was getting monthly salary of Rs.20,000/.

sentences.text: 2 Petitioner No.1 is the wife, petitioner No.2 is the minor kid and petitioners No.3 and 4 are the parents of deceased.

The Peenya Traffic police have registered the case against the driver of Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA43 5119, in Cr.No.137/2020 for the offence punishable U/Sec.279, 338 and 304(A) of IPC, Sec.134 (a & b), Sec.187 of IMV Act.
With these averments petitioners prayed to allow the petition.
3. In response to the notice issued by the Tribunal, the 1st respondent appeared through its counsel and filed written statement.
In so for as the 2 nd respondent is concerned, he being the R.C. owner of the offending vehicle remained absent, hence he was placed Exparte.

4. The written statement averments of 1st respondent is as hereunder:
Respondent No.1Insurance Company has denied the entire averments of the petition.
It is contended that, the petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties.
The rider of Motor Cycle bearing No.KA19EY8857 was riding the vehicle without wearing helmet and without driving licence at the time of accident.

This respondent has denied the involvement of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA435119 in the accident,
rash and negligent driving of said lorry by its driver, age, occupation and income of deceased.
It is contended that, the driver of offending lorry was driven the same carefully and cautiously on the correct side of the road.
The accident took place solely due to rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle by its rider.

The 1 st respondent has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to offending lorry,
however contended that, liability is subject to terms and conditions of the policy.

It is contended that, the 2nd respondent has breached the policy conditions as he has willfully entrusted his vehicle to the person who did not possess valid and effective driving licence to the drive the same on the date of accident.

Further contended that,
the rider of motor cycle bearing Reg.No.KA19EY8857 also contributed higher degree of negligence to the cause of accident.
The claim made by the petitioners is excessive and exorbitant.
With these averments, the 1st respondent has prayed to dismiss the petition.

5. On the basis of above pleadings, the predecessor in the office has framed the following:
: I S S U E S:
1.

Whether petitioners prove that Ratna Ram was died on 26.11.2020 in a road traffic accident caused by the rash and negligent driving of driver of Tipper Lorry bearing Registration No.KA435119 as stated in the petition?
2. Whether the petitioners prove the age and income of the deceased?

Hence, they have taken together for common discussion in order to avoid repetition.
9. It is the case of the petitioners that, on 26.11.2020 at about 9.20 am., deceased Ratna Ram was proceeding as a rider on the two wheeler bearing Reg.No.KA19EY8857.

While he reached near Spirit Zone, T. Dasarahalli on NH4 Tumkur road, Bengaluru, the Tipper Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA435119 driven by its driver from behind, rash and negligently, in a Zigzag manner and dashed to the aforesaid two wheeler. Due to impact, deceased fell down, wheel of lorry ran over his head and he succumbed to injuries on the spot.
To prove their contention, petitioners have lead oral and documentary evidence.

Further case of the petitioners is that, the deceased was aged about 22 years and he was working as Sales Executive at Pipe Chem Indujstries, Peenya Industrial Area,
Bengaluru and getting salary of Rs.20,000/ per month.

It is the case of the petitioners that, the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of the driver of Lorry bearing Reg.No.KA435119 and in this regard, the Peenya Traffic police have registered the case and field charge sheet against the said driver.
10.
In order to prove the claim of petitioners, the petitioner No.1 was examined as P.W.1 by filing affidavit.
P.W.1 also produced as many as 20 documents, which have been marked as Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.20.
Ex.P.Series Ex.P.1 is the true copy of FIR in Cr.No.137/2020 pertaining to Peenya Traffic PS.
Ex. P.2
is the true copy of complaint.
Ex. P.3
is the true copy of Spot Mahazar.
Ex.P.4 is the true copy of Spot Sketch.
Ex.P.5 is the true copy of M.V.A. Report.
Ex.P.6 is the true copy of inquest report.
Ex.P.7 is the true copy of P.M. Report.
Ex. P.8
is the true copy of Charge Sheet.
Ex . P.9
is the Coffin Maker Certificate (Sealing Certificate of Dead Body).
Ex.P.10 is the Certificate of Embalming.
Ex.P.11 is the notarized copy of Aadhaar Card of deceased Ratna Ram.
Ex.P.12 is the notarized copy of 2 marks card of Ratna Ram issued by Board of Secondary Education, Rajasthan.
Ex . P.13
is the notarized copy of Aadhaar Card of Kamla Kumari.
Ex.P.14 is the notarized copy of Birth Certificate of petitioner No.2.
Ex.P.15 is the notarized copy of Aadhaar Card of Bhagirth.
Ex.P.16 is the notarized copy of Aadhaar Card of Chuni.
Ex.P.17 is the Air Way bill.
Ex.P.18 is the Salary Certificate of Ratna Ram.
Ex.P.19 are the 9 Salary Slips of Ratna Ram.
Ex.P.20 is the copy of Statement of Account of Ratna Ram.
11. According to the respondent No.1, the Tipper Lorry in question was not involved in the accident nor caused injuries to the deceased.
The driver of lorry driving the said vehicle carefully and cautiously on the correct side of the road.
The accident took place due to negligent riding of the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA19EY8857 by its rider.
The deceased has contributed higher degree of negligence to the cause of accident.
There was no negligence on the part of the driver of the Tipper Lorry.
The petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties.
12. Before going to discuss the issues, it is appropriate to say the admitted facts of the case.
There is no dispute with regard to death of Ratna Ram in the road traffic accident.
The respondent No.1 has not seriously disputed the relationship of petitioners with deceased Ratna Ram.

13. So, now the important question before this Tribunal is to find out whether the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle or not and whether the deceased has contributed the negligence for the alleged accident or not?
In order to answer these aspects, it is appropriate to take Ex.P.1 to Ex.P.8.
On careful perusal of these documents, it is clear that, criminal case was registered against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Apart from that, charge sheet was submitted against the driver of the offending vehicle as per Ex.P.8.

It is relevant to note that, though the respondent No.1 has contended that, accident was occurred due to the negligence of the deceased, however, in order to substantiate the same, the 1 st respondent has not placed any material before this Tribunal.
Further, the 1st respondent has not endeavor to examine the driver of the offending vehicle.

At this juncture it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka between National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Krishnappa and Another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, "the rider of the offending vehicle was Kamala Kumari vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65138908/
5 not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scootrist".

At the cost of repetition,
the Investigation Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle bearing No.KA435119.

Therefore, it is manifest that, the materials placed on record by the petitioners is sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent driving of driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA435119.
Apart from that, the 1st respondent has contended that, deceased was not wearing helmet and he had no driving licence as on the date of accident.

At this juncture itself it is worth to rely on the decision of Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka, Dharwad Bench in M.F.A. 101144/2020 between Anand Vs. Arjun and Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka interpreted Sec.129 of IMV Act and held that, "non wearing of helmet is not a ground to deny the compensation".

sentences.text: Further, the Hon'ble Apex Court in Sudhir Kumar Rana Vs. Surinder Singh and Others held that, "mere non possessing of D.L. cannot be held to be guilty of contributory negligence.

sentences.text: To put it differently if a person drives a vehicle without a licence, he commits an offence.

The same by itself may not lead to a finding of negligence as regards the accident".
14.
Now, the next aspect is with regard to age of the deceased.
In the instant case, the respondent No.1 has disputed the age, occupation and income of the deceased.
According to the petitioners, the deceased was aged about 22 years.

In order to substantiate the same, P.W.1 has produced the notarized copy of Aadhaar Card of deceased, which is marked as Ex.P.11 and notarized copy of Marks Card of deceased, which is marked as Ex.P.12.
On careful perusal of these documents, it reveals that, the date of birth of deceased is 01.05.1998.
The accident was occurred on 26.11.2020.
During the course of crossexamination P.W.1, she has deposed that, at the time of accident deceased was aged 22 years.
Therefore, age of the deceased is considered as 22 years at the time of accident.
15. Now, the next aspect is with respect to income of deceased.

According to the petitioners, the deceased was working as a Sales Executive at Pipe Chem Industries, No.3/4, 1st Main, Peenya 1st Stage, 1st Main road, Peenya Industrial Area, Bengaluru and getting salary of Rs.20,000/ per month at the time of his death.
However, to substantiate the income of the deceased, P.W.1 has produced Salary Certificate at Ex.P.18 and 9 Salary Slips of deceased at Ex.P.19.
On perusal of these documents, it appears to this Tribunal that, the deceased Ratna Ram was working as Sales Executive at PipeChem Industries and his salary is Rs.20,000/ per month.
Further, on perusal of salary slips, this Tribunal do not find any deductions with respect to Provident Fund and E.S.I.
Apart from that, P.W.1 has also produced the Account Statement of deceased at Ex.P.20.

On perusal of Ex.P.20,
it appears to this Tribunal that, on 08.06.2020, i.e., prior to the date of accident, Rs.2,00,000/ has been credited to the account of the deceased.
It is not forthcoming from the side of petitioners why Rs.2,00,000/ was credited to the account of deceased.
Therefore, the credit of Rs.2,00,000/ to the account of deceased is not a salary.

That apart, during the course of crossexamination of P.W.1,
the counsel for the 1st respondent has stoutly denied the avocation of deceased.
Under such circumstances, it is the primary duty of the petitioners to examine the employer of deceased.
However, in the instant case, the petitioners have not examined the employer.
Why they have not examined the employer is not forthcoming from the side of petitioners.

Further it appears to this Tribunal that, Ex.P.18 and Ex.P.19 are not the genuine documents and same will not come to the aid of petitioners to substantiate that, the deceased was working as Sales Executive.

Hence, this Kamala Kumari vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65138908/
6 Tribunal can inferred that, at the time of accident, the deceased was not working as Sales Executive.

At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka decided in M.F.A. No.101144 of 2020 ( MVI) on 05.07.2023, between Ananda Vs. Arun and Another, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka at Para 9 (b) as hereunder:
"
In the absence of any cogent material on record, it is for the courts and Tribunals to assess the income notionally.
The notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident of the year 2017 is Rs.10,250/.

In the absence of any material produced by the claimant to prove his income, it is appropriate to assess the notional income of the injured claimant at Rs.10,250/ per month, and the same is assessed as the monthly income of the injured claimant".
16. In the instant case also, the petitioners though they have produced salary certificate and salary slips, the non examination of employer creates doubt on the avocation of the deceased.
Apart from that, Ex.
P.18 to Ex.P.20, there are no documents to come to the conclusion that, the deceased was working as a Sales Executive.

As such in the absence of authentic documents and supportive evidence, the notional income of the deceased is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2020 is Rs.14,500/ per month.
It is pertinent to note that, the accident took place on 26.11.2020.
Hence, the notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.14,500/ per month.
17. Now the next aspect is whether the respondent No.1 has proved that the petition is bad for non joinder of necessary parties.

On careful perusal of the objection statement of respondent No.1,
except bare contention regarding nonjoinder of necessary parties, there is no materials to substantiate the same from the side of 1 st respondent.

Already this Tribunal has observed that,
there is no contributory negligence from the side of deceased.
Further this Tribunal has already observed that, the accident caused due to rash or negligence driving of the driver of offending vehicle.
Therefore, the respondent No.1 has failed to prove that the petition is bad for nonjoinder of necessary parties.
Accordingly, Issue No.1 is answered in the Affirmative and Issue No.2 is answered in the partly Affirmative, Issue No.3 and Issue No.4 are answered in the Negative .
18. ISSUE No.5: This issue is with regard to entitlement of relief.
According to the petition averments, petitioner No.1 is the wife of deceased, petitioner No.2 is the minor daughter, petitioner No.3 is the father and petitioner No.4 is the mother of deceased.
The 1st petitioner has lost her husband.
2nd petitioner has lost her loving father at their tender age.
3rd and 4th petitioners being the parents of deceased have lost their son at their old age.
Moreover, the bond between the parents and children is an eternal.
Hence, petitioner Nos.1 to 4 are considered as dependents of deceased.
Keeping in view of the 4 dependents of deceased in the case on hand, 1/4 th of the amount is to be deducted from total income toward the personal expenses of deceased.

19. Already this Tribunal has observed that, the petitioners have established the age of deceased i.e.,
as on the date of accident the deceased was aged about 22 years.

The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, held that "if the person died in the motor Kamala Kumari vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65138908/
7 accident, the income with respect to the future prospects has to be taken into consideration while awarding compensation".

entities.text: National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text:
It is relevant to note that The Hon'ble Apex Court has provided the chart for the age of the deceased and percentage of future prospects as hereunder:
"If the deceased is self employed or fixed salary, his age below 40 years, future prospects is 40%".
"If the deceased between 40 to 50 years age, future prospects is 25%".

"If the deceased between 50 to 60 years age, future prospects is 10% and if the deceased more than 60 years, no addition as future prospects".
20.
Admittedly, the petitioners have produced documents to show the income of deceased.
However, this Tribunal declined to consider those salary slips.
Hence, the deceased is not a permanent job holder and he is not a fixed salary person.
The deceased was aged about 22 years and therefore, additional income is added to the income towards future prospects.

In the instant case,
the deceased was 22 years.
Hence, the future prospects of 40% is to be added to the income of deceased.
By applying the principles of above ruling 40% of the Rs.14,500/ has to be added to monthly income of deceased, which comes to Rs.5,800/.
So, monthly income of deceased is taken at Rs.14,500/ + Rs.5,800/ = Rs.20,300/.
In this case petitioner Nos.1 to 4 are considered as dependents of deceased.
Keeping in view of the 4 dependents of deceased in the case on hand, 1/4th amount is to be deducted toward personal expenses.
From this his personal living expenses which should be 1/4th of Rs.20,300/ has to be deducted.
Thereby, the actual income will come to Rs.20,300 - Rs.5,075/ =Rs.15,225/.

Then total income of the deceased per annum comes to Rs.1,82,700/ (Rs.15,225 x 12 =1,82,700/)
21.
As the deceased was 22 years old at the time of death, the multiplier 18 is applied, which is appropriate to age of deceased.
The normal compensation would then workout to be Rs.1,82,700 x 18 = Rs.32,88,600/ for loss of dependency.

22. The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others has laid down the guidelines with regard to awarding compensation towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and consortium.

sentences.text: The petitioners have contended that, they have spent substantial amount towards transportation of dead body and funeral expenses.
In order to substantiate the same, P.W.1 has produced Coffin Maker Certificate (Sealing Certificate of Dead Body) as Ex.P.9 and Air Waybill as Ex.P.17.
On perusal of these documents it appears that, the petitioners have air lifted the dead body of deceased to their native place by paying Rs.11,274.90 and it is rounded off to Rs.11,275/.
Now the question before this Tribunal is whether petitioners No.2 to 4 are also entitled for consortium or not?
Admittedly, the 1st petitioner is the wife and she is entitled for spousal consortium.
Admittedly the petitioner No.2 is the minor daughter of deceased.
Petitioner Nos.3 and 4 are the parents of deceased.
At this juncture, it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble Apex Court reported in 2018 (1) SCC 130 between Magma General Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Nanuram @ Churu Ram and Others.

Further, Rs.16,500/ is awarded for funeral expenses and also Rs.16,500/ is awarded towards loss of estate.
Further, as per Ex.P.17, the dead body of deceased has been airlifted and the petitioners have spend Rs.11,275/.
Hence, Rs.11,275/ is awarded towards transportation of dead body.

Hence, petitioners are entitled for just and reasonable amount of Rs.35,08,875/.
24.
Regarding liability and interest.
Driving License: Charge sheet submitted by IO does not reveals that driver of offending vehicle was driving the vehicle without valid and effective DL.
Hence, it is held that, the driver of offending vehicle was holding valid and effective D.L. as on the date of alleged accident.
Insurance Policy and liability:
Respondent No.1 the insurance company has admitted the issuance of insurance policy with respect to offending vehicle.
Hence, it is held that, insurance coverage of the vehicle was in force at the time of accident.
Hence, the respondent No.1 shall pay compensation amount to the petitioners.
Interest:

In view of the decision reported in MFA NO:
301312019 dtd, 12.5.2020, rate of interest on the compensation amount is awarded at 6% p.a. from the date of petition till realization.
Accordingly, this Tribunal is answered Issue No.5 in Partly Affirmative.
25. ISSUE No.6:.
In view of discussion made above, this Tribunal proceed to pass the following.

sentences.text: Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners U/Sec.166 of M.V. Act is partly allowed with costs of the Petition.

Petitioners are awarded just and  reasonable compensation of Rs.35,08,875/ (Rupees Thirty Five Lakhs, Eight Thousand Eight Hundred and Seventy Five Only) with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of petition to till the date of depositing of the compensation amount in the court.

Respondent No.1 being insurer of the offending vehicle is liable to pay the compensation amount to the petitioners and directed to deposit the compensation amount awarded to the petitioners in the Tribunal within 2 months from the date of this judgment.
Draw award accordingly.

Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/. : APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION :
On deposit of compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for 40%, petitioner No.2 is entitled for 30% and petitioner No.3 and 4 are entitled for 15% each with interest.

It is clarified that, the 1st petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
with interest is to be paid to them through Epayment on proper identification as per rules.
Entire share of petitioner No.2 with interest shall be invested in F.D. in her name in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank until she attains the age of majority.

13. So, now the important question before this Tribunal is to find out whether the accident occurred due to rash or negligent driving of offending vehicle or not and whether the deceased has contributed the negligence for the alleged accident or not?
opennyai_summary.ANALYSIS:
The accident took place due to negligent riding of the Motor Cycle bearing Reg.No.KA19EY8857 by its rider.
On careful perusal of these documents, it is clear that, criminal case was registered against the driver of the offending vehicle.
Apart from that, charge sheet was submitted against the driver of the offending vehicle as per Ex.P.8.
Further, the 1st respondent has not endeavor to examine the driver of the offending vehicle.
At this juncture it is worth to rely on the decision of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka between National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Krishnappa and Another reported in 2001 ACJ 1105, wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka held that, "the rider of the offending vehicle was Kamala Kumari vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65138908/
5 not examined to prove any contributory negligence on the part of scootrist".
At the cost of repetition,
the Investigation Officer has filed charge sheet against the driver of offending vehicle bearing No.KA435119.
Therefore, it is manifest that, the materials placed on record by the petitioners is sufficient to believe that, the accident took place due to rash or negligent driving of driver of the offending vehicle bearing Reg.No.KA435119.
Apart from that, the 1st respondent has contended that, deceased was not wearing helmet and he had no driving licence as on the date of accident.
Therefore, the credit of Rs.2,00,000/ to the account of deceased is not a salary.
Under such circumstances, it is the primary duty of the petitioners to examine the employer of deceased.
However, in the instant case, the petitioners have not examined the employer.
Why they have not examined the employer is not forthcoming from the side of petitioners.
Further it appears to this Tribunal that, Ex.P.18 and Ex.P.19 are not the genuine documents and same will not come to the aid of petitioners to substantiate that, the deceased was working as Sales Executive.
Hence, this Kamala Kumari vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65138908/
6 Tribunal can inferred that, at the time of accident, the deceased was not working as Sales Executive.
16. In the instant case also, the petitioners though they have produced salary certificate and salary slips, the non examination of employer creates doubt on the avocation of the deceased.
P.18 to Ex.P.20, there are no documents to come to the conclusion that, the deceased was working as a Sales Executive.
As such in the absence of authentic documents and supportive evidence, the notional income of the deceased is to be considered by relying on the judgment of the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka referred to above.
As per the notional income fixed by the Karnataka State Legal Service Authority for the accident in the year 2020 is Rs.14,500/ per month.
Hence, the notional income of the deceased is considered as Rs.14,500/ per month.
On careful perusal of the objection statement of respondent No.1,
except bare contention regarding nonjoinder of necessary parties, there is no materials to substantiate the same from the side of 1 st respondent.
Moreover, the bond between the parents and children is an eternal.
Hence, petitioner Nos.1 to 4 are considered as dependents of deceased.
Keeping in view of the 4 dependents of deceased in the case on hand, 1/4 th of the amount is to be deducted from total income toward the personal expenses of deceased.
The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co. Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others, held that "if the person died in the motor Kamala Kumari vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65138908/
7 accident, the income with respect to the future prospects has to be taken into consideration while awarding compensation".
Admittedly, the petitioners have produced documents to show the income of deceased.
Hence, the deceased is not a permanent job holder and he is not a fixed salary person.
The deceased was aged about 22 years and therefore, additional income is added to the income towards future prospects.
In the instant case,
the deceased was 22 years.
Hence, the future prospects of 40% is to be added to the income of deceased.
22. The Hon'ble Apex Court in National Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others has laid down the guidelines with regard to awarding compensation towards loss of estate, funeral expenses and consortium.
On perusal of these documents it appears that, the petitioners have air lifted the dead body of deceased to their native place by paying Rs.11,274.90 and it is rounded off to Rs.11,275/.
Admittedly, the 1st petitioner is the wife and she is entitled for spousal consortium.
It is relevant to note that, the Hon'ble Apex Court in National Kamala Kumari vs Hdfc Ergo General Ins Co Ltd on 14 June, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/65138908/
8 Insurance Co.Ltd., Vs. Pranay Sethi and Others Case, observed that, the conventional heads namely filial consortium, loss of estate, funeral expenses has to be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.

Therefore, the 1 st petitioner is entitled for Rs.44,000/ under the head of spousal consortium and petitioner Nos.2 to 4 are entitled for Rs.44,000/ each under the head of filial consortium.
Further, Rs.16,500/ is awarded for funeral expenses and also Rs.16,500/ is awarded towards loss of estate.
Further, as per Ex.P.17, the dead body of deceased has been airlifted and the petitioners have spend Rs.11,275/.
Hence, Rs.11,275/ is awarded towards transportation of dead body.

Draw award accordingly.
Advocate fee is fixed at Rs.1,000/. : APPORTIONMENT OF COMPENSATION :
On deposit of compensation amount, Petitioner No.1 is entitled for 40%, petitioner No.2 is entitled for 30% and petitioner No.3 and 4 are entitled for 15% each with interest.
60% of share of petitioner No.1 with interest is to be paid to her by way of E payment on proper identification as per rules and after verifying the stay order from the Hon'ble Appellate Court and remaining 40% of her share with interest shall be invested in F.D. in her name in any nationalized bank or scheduled bank of her choice for a period of 3 years.
It is clarified that, the 1st petitioner is at liberty to withdraw the periodical interest accrued on her deposit amount from time to time.
with interest is to be paid to them through Epayment on proper identification as per rules.
